**Update to #63:** The KV cache reuse mechanism in `server-context.cpp` around line 2839 works as a chunk-based LCP (Longest Common Prefix) system. It scans cached prompt tokens against the new prompt tokens, finds the longest matching prefix, then uses `common_context_seq_rm` and `common_context_seq_add` to physically shift matching KV cache chunks to new positions. The `n_cache_reuse` parameter (configurable per-request) gates minimum chunk size. When aLora activation points exist (`slot.alora_invocation_start`), `n_past` is capped to prevent caching past adapter boundaries. Cache mismatches are diagnosed by printing token strings around the miss point. This is distinct from the *prompt cache* (in-memory deduplication in `server-task.cpp`) and *slot save/restore* (file-based KV serialization).
